$comment: Modules that were NOT type-clean when src/worker/lib became TypeScript.
Each carries a `// @ts-nocheck` header pointing here.
THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK. A contract test asserts that the set of files
carrying @ts-nocheck is exactly the set named here, so adding one is a
deliberate edit somebody reviews rather than a quiet opt-out, and fixing a
module means deleting its entry. The counts are what tsc reported the day
the conversion landed, kept so progress is measurable rather than asserted.
THE ERRORS WERE EXPOSED BY THE CONVERSION, NOT INTRODUCED BY IT. JavaScript
treated parameters as optional and inferred object shapes loosely; TypeScript
made those call-arity and unknown-property assumptions visible.
57 of 69 Worker modules are fully checked. The other 12 are named below; the
answer was not to relax the compiler for the whole directory.
ENFORCED by a contract test: the set of files carrying @ts-nocheck must equal
the set named here. The same test checks the totals, and a separate contract
compares `tsc --listFilesOnly` with every Worker .ts file so the scope cannot
silently drift back to an obsolete extension.
